chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abd al-Malik ibn Utbah said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about a man from whom I buy food or buy goods, on the condition that I have no defect/liability from him. Is this valid? And how is it valid? And what is its limit? He said, 'It is not proper.'

key_terms.وَضِيعَةٌ: Defect or liability (in the context of goods)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying goods with a condition of no defect in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) addresses the validity of conditional sales (*bay' al-ta'liq*) where the buyer purchases food or goods with the stipulation that there be no defect (*wadhe'ah*). The Imam’s ruling that it is 'not proper' (*la yanbaghi*) reflects the Shia juristic preference for avoiding ambiguity (*gharar*) in trade contracts, ensuring that the condition is clearly defined and enforceable to prevent disputes. This highlights the emphasis on transparency and fairness in commercial transactions within Islamic law.
